programs.name: Anterior hip + strength rebuild
programs.short_description: For lifters with a history of anterior-hip / groin irritation who want to rebuild squat and deadlift base without provoking symptoms.
programs.who_this_is_for: You've had episodes of hip flexor / groin pain that flared under squatting or Metcons. You want to keep training seriously — not stop. This program is your barbell arc built around what your hip can actually take.
programs.what_youll_achieve: A 12-month strength arc with structured re-introduction, three progressive 5/3/1 cycles, a Hatch specialisation block, and a peak test. Provocative positions are respected throughout. Ends with a specialist-ready report of your symptom + load history.
programs.retest: Cycle-end 5-rep max on primary lifts (squat, block pull) with symptom review. Every 4 weeks.

programs.name: Engine Builder — Block 1: Base
programs.short_description: Block 1 of a 3-block, ~6-month engine transformation. Eight weeks of Zone 1/2 base with a single weekly hard session added in week 4. Row, bike, ski-erg, or run.
programs.who_this_is_for: You've got okay strength but your engine is the thing holding you back — a metcon at 15 minutes falls apart, a 5k feels harder than it should, HR runs away at moderate pace. You want a plan that actually builds the base rather than chasing intervals from day one.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Block 1 of a 6-month engine transformation. In these 8 weeks: 5-8% VO2max improvement, a measurable resting HR drop (5-10 bpm typical), and — most importantly — the aerobic base that lets Block 2 (volume) and Block 3 (polarised) actually work. Modality is your choice at intake: row, bike, ski-erg, or run. Weeks 1-4 are low-impact regardless; running introduces at week 5 if that's your goal.
programs.retest: Week 8 midweek. Repeat everything you measured at intake: resting HR (3-morning average), 5-minute submax HR at your intake pace, plus 500m row TT and/or 1km run TT if applicable. Rest HR and submax HR are always measurable — they're the honest answer to 'did the block work'.

programs.name: Handstand Walk
programs.adapts: Intake picks your tier; drills and phase pace adapt to your capability.
programs.short_description: Multi-tiered handstand walk program from wall-supported beginner to advanced turns and obstacles. Personalised sessions target your specific weak capabilities.
programs.who_this_is_for: You want to handstand walk. Some athletes can't hold a wall handstand yet; some walk 10m+ but can't turn; the app meets you where you are and builds each sub-capability separately.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Block 1 of a multi-block arc. Beginners: consistent wall handstand + brief freestand attempts. Wall-holders: first freestand hold + first walk step. Freestanders: 3-5 continuous walk steps. Advanced: first pirouette or obstacle traverse.
programs.retest: Weekly retest of freestand hold time; every 4 weeks: full assessment (wall hold, freestand, walk distance, wrist symptom score).
programs.load_hint: ~1.5-2 hr/week (5 sessions/wk, 4 on Foundation, 15-18 min each)

programs.name: Concurrent-Strength Maintenance
prerequisites: A known current back-squat 5RM — the program's whole promise is that this number doesn't fall.
At least some prior cardio exposure — you can hold Z1 pace for 15 min without HR runaway.
programs.short_description: For lifters adding cardio without losing the squat. Explosive-strength cost bounded, cited, PR-banned.
programs.who_this_is_for: You have a documented strength floor you'd rather not lose. You want aerobic capacity. Traditional 5/3/1 fights with running; this program bounds the cost against Schumann 2022's SMD data.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Submax HR down 8-15 bpm at fixed pace, back squat / block pull / front squat maintained within 2.5 kg of pre-block TM, RPE ceiling 7 throughout (Schumann 2022 explosive-strength discipline).
programs.retest: Cycle-end 5RM confirm + submax HR at row pace-5. At week 8 (end of block).

programs.name: Rowing 2K Test Prep
prerequisites: An existing Z2 aerobic base — either you've been rowing / cycling / running easy for 4+ weeks recently, or you've completed the Engine Builder program.
programs.short_description: For rowers chasing the 2K PR. Six weeks, cited, tapered — no more than that.
programs.who_this_is_for: You've built a Z2 base (or you've completed Engine Builder). Now you want to PR the 2K.
programs.what_youll_achieve: 2K down 3-30 seconds by tier. Threshold pace shifted 3-6%. Race-day taper baked in.
programs.retest: 2K test every 2 weeks. Full test at week 6.

programs.name: Overhead Mobility
programs.adapts: Intake picks your tier; drill selection and progression pace adapt to your ROM.
programs.short_description: Shoulder + thoracic + scap sequence for stronger snatch, OHS, and press. Kinematic base before load.
programs.who_this_is_for: You want to snatch, OHS, or press without impingement — but your arms don't reach vertical loaded. Or they do, but only barely.
programs.what_youll_achieve: By week 10: loaded shoulder flexion at 180°, empty-bar OHS to parallel or better, first snatch-grip Sotts press. Retest via goniometer + OHS depth.
programs.retest: Supine shoulder flexion + OHS depth ratio at phase-end (weeks 3, 7, 10).

programs.name: First Strict Pull-Up
programs.adapts: Intake picks your tier; drills adapt weekly to your weakest capability (grip, scap, row, negative).
programs.short_description: Multi-tier skill program on the shared pull drill library. Grip → scap → negative → band → unassisted, then volume. Personalised sessions target your weakest sub-capability first.
programs.who_this_is_for: You want a strict pull-up. Some athletes can't dead-hang 15 seconds yet; some do 1-2 reps and want to hit 5. The app meets you where you are and builds each sub-capability separately. Not for kipping pull-ups — that's a different skill.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Beginners: 25-45 second dead hang, clean scap pulls, first ring rows. Assisted-only lifters: first strict rep from a 10-second negative. First-repper: 3-5 unbroken. Volume tier: 8-10 unbroken with wide-grip variety unlocked.
programs.retest: Weekly max-rep retest (Tier C/D) or weekly hang-time retest (Tier A/B); every 4 weeks: full assessment (dead hang, scap pull, ring row, strict pull-up, negative control).

programs.name: Muscle-Up Acquisition (strict ring)
programs.adapts: Intake gates on prerequisites (3+ strict pull-ups, 3+ ring dips), then picks your tier by muscle-up experience.
prerequisites: 3+ strict pull-ups (no kip, no swing, dead hang to chin over bar).
3+ strict ring dips (support → 90° elbow → lockout, no leg swing).
If either is below the threshold, intake routes you to First Strict Pull-Up or an equivalent dip build first.
programs.short_description: Multi-tier strict ring muscle-up program. False-grip base, transition mechanics, ring dip strength. Not for kipping muscle-ups — different skill, different program.
programs.who_this_is_for: You have your strict pull-ups and ring dips and now want the strict ring muscle-up. The transition is the bottleneck — not the pull, not the dip. This program isolates it: seated-band, low-ring negatives, jump-assist, first strict attempt.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Prep tier: 3-5 strict ring dips, 15s false-grip hang. Transition tier: seated-band mastered, first low-ring muscle-up, first strict attempt week 8-10. First Rep tier: 2-3 strict ring muscle-ups unbroken with weighted-preview singles.
programs.retest: Weekly max-rep retest (Tier C) or false-grip hang + ring dip retest (Tier A/B); every 4 weeks: full assessment battery.

programs.name: Engine Builder — Block 2: Volume
programs.adapts: Intake gates on Block 1 completion (or equivalent base) and picks tier by current cardio hours + Block 1 delta.
prerequisites: Engine Builder Block 1 completed within the last 4 weeks OR an equivalent 8-week aerobic base (5+ hrs/week cardio, can hold Z1 for 75+ min).
Chest-strap HR monitor strongly recommended — half the block's target zones sit in the range where wrist-optical HR drops out.
programs.short_description: Block 2 of the 3-block engine transformation. Two hard sessions per week on top of a rising Z1 volume floor. Threshold pace shift is the headline metric.
programs.who_this_is_for: You finished Block 1 (or have an equivalent base) and want to keep going. Block 2 is where the majority of VO2max and threshold gains land — but only after the base is in. This is a sharp-end block: two hard sessions per week, more time, more intensity.
programs.what_youll_achieve: Threshold pace / power shift 2-5% by tier. Additional VO2max +4-9% on top of Block 1. Submax HR at fixed pace additional -3 to -8 bpm. Retest at week 4 (mid-block check) and week 8-10 (end-of-block).
programs.retest: 20-min TT + submax HR at fixed pace at week 4 and week 8-10. Modality-specific TT (2K row / 5K run) at end-of-block if applicable.
programs.physical_test_prerequisite: Fresh 20-min TT within the last 4 weeks OR schedule one in week 1 Wednesday.
